newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solana says will miss Joulwan as top NATO soldier.
newsitem.headline: Solana says will miss Joulwan as top NATO soldier.

text.p: NATO Secretary General Javier Solana said on Tuesday he would miss the "wise counsel" of NATO's top soldier General George Joulwan when he retires in June and that he had served with distinction.

Solana said in a statement he had been informed by Joulwan, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander, Europe (SACEUR), he would retire after 36 years of active duty service. The retirement was announced by the White House on December 24.

"He has served with distinction as SACEUR during a particularly challenging period for the alliance and I will miss his wise counsel and extremely effective leadership after he leaves this summer," the statement said.

U.S. President Bill Clinton has not yet mentioned a successor to Joulwan, a career soldier who reluctantly accepted the NATO post in October 1993 when General John Shalikashvili, also an American, left NATO to become chief of staff for Clinton.
As NATO's top military officer, Joulwan oversaw the NATO air strikes in 1995 which helped bring Bosnian Serbs to the negotiating table.
Since the Dayton peace accords late last year Joulwan has played a vital role in trying to ensure the fragile peace in Bosnia overseeing the NATO-led peace implementation force IFOR there.
